# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👍 👉 👍 ✌ 👎 👉 👎 ✌ ✋ 👉 ☝ ✌ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🫴]

**Thinking.** I am Deaf: I see the bomb, I can speak to both teammates, my gestures reach only Mute. What I see: display shows 0, one light and it is red, three wires — 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. This turn I received gestures from both teammates. Blind sent a wave, a point at me, an open palm — "hello, you, give me" — Blind is asking for information, and Blind can hear my voice, so a spoken broadcast covers them. Mute sent fourteen gestures with no shared code established; I can spot a loose pattern (three items each marked by the pointing-right hand, ending in index/two/OK), but guessing a wire-cut instruction from an unagreed code is exactly how bombs go off. The critical structural fact: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so I am the only bridge from the manual to the hands. The path to an answer is: I broadcast the bomb facts, Mute reads the manual with those facts in mind, Mute sends me the instruction in a code we fix right now, I relay it to Blind by voice. So this turn I define a minimal, unambiguous gesture code with Mute (finger-count for wire number, thumbs up/down for cut/leave, point-up for "need more facts"), acknowledge their contact, and ask Blind for a tactile inventory so nothing on the bomb goes unnoticed. Nobody touches anything until a rule arrives.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, I see the bomb. Report: the display reads 0. There is one light and it is red. There are three wires; number them 1, 2, 3 from my left to my right: wire 1 blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. Blind, your wave reached me. Nobody cuts or presses anything yet. Blind, feel the bomb and speak back: are there batteries, buttons, or any parts beyond the display, the light, and the three wires?")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I saw your fourteen gestures, but we share no code yet and I will not guess at a wire. Fix this code with me: gesture the wire number first, where index finger means 1, two fingers means 2, and the OK sign means 3; then thumbs up means cut it and thumbs down means leave it. If you need more facts about the bomb, point up and I will answer next round. Thumbs up from me means received and agreed. You now have my spoken report: display 0, red light, wires blue, green, red. Remember Blind cannot see gestures, so send me the manual's rule and I will relay it to Blind by voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👆 🤞 👉 ✌ 👍 ✊ 👉 👌 👍 ✋ 👉 ☝ 👍 👆 🤞 ✊ ✋ 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 🫳 ☝]

**Thinking.** First, the critical change: the light has gone from RED to WHITE since last round, while the display held at 0 and the wires are untouched. Mute composed their answer based on my stale report of a red light, so any light-dependent rule may be void — I must not relay cuts until Mute re-checks against white.

Parsing Mute's message under our agreed code: the clear units are "two fingers + thumbs up" (cut wire 2), "OK sign + thumbs up" (cut wire 3), and "open palm + right-point + index + thumbs up", which I read as "leave wire 1" — likely "cut 2, then 3, not 1". But their opening trio (index up, crossed fingers, fist) and the lone fist are undefined, so the parse is provisional. I also made a code error last round: I assigned the single index finger both "wire 1" and "need more facts". Fixing that now: index = wire 1 only, wave = need info.

Topology check: I receive nobody's speech (I'm deaf), so Blind rightly gestured to me instead of speaking — my turn-1 request for Blind to "speak back" was useless and I should own that. But Blind and Mute share a live channel I can't hear: Blind speaks, Mute listens. So the efficient loop is: Blind asks the manual question aloud to Mute; Mute answers me in gesture code; I relay by voice to Blind. I'll set that up, ask Mute for the rule for *every* light colour so we stop losing rounds, and hold Blind from touching anything.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you listen. State update: since last round the light has changed from red to white. The display still reads 0. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Nobody has touched the bomb. Mute: your instruction was built on a red light, so nothing is relayed yet. Re-check the manual for a white light, and if the rule depends on light colour, send me the rule for every colour it lists so we stop losing rounds. Also confirm my reading of your message: cut wire 2, then wire 3, and leave wire 1 alone. I did not understand your opening three signs or the lone fist; if I misread anything, re-send just that part. One code fix: the single index finger now means only wire 1; when you need more facts from me, wave instead. Blind: I am deaf, so your voice never reaches me, your hands do, and you chose right to sign. New plan: you and Mute share a channel I cannot hear, Blind speaks and Mute listens. So ask Mute out loud right now: what does the manual say for a white light, display 0, wires blue, green, red. Mute answers me in our gesture code and I relay it to you by voice. For signing to me use the code you already heard from me: single finger is wire 1, two fingers wire 2, the OK sign wire 3, thumbs up cut, thumbs down leave. I guess your last four signs meant there is one button on the bomb: if that is right, answer me with the handshake sign; if wrong, thumbs down and then show me what you meant. Until I say go, touch nothing and cut nothing.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👆 ✋ 👆 🤞 👉 ✌ 👍 👆 ✊ 👉 👌 👍 👆 ✋ 👉 ☝ 👍 🙏 👋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👋 🫳 ☝]

**Thinking.** The light changed again — white to green, after red to white. It cycles every round while the display holds at 0, so colour-keyed rules need the whole table, not one row. Parsing Mute's message against the hypothesis I now believe: the signs 🤞 ✊ ✋ are being used as colours (crossed fingers = green, fist = red, open palm = white), each followed by pointing-right, a wire number, and thumbs up. That reads as a rule table: green→cut 2, red→cut 3, white→cut 1 — a much better fit than my old "cut 2 then 3" guess, which their leading thumbs-down appears to reject. Their closing wave, under my code, means they still need facts — almost certainly things only Blind can feel, like batteries. Blind's message starts with thumbs down: my "one button" guess was wrong, and they re-sent palm-down plus one finger, which I still can't decode — I'll binary-question it. The plan: broadcast the green state, confirm the colour table and colour code with Mute, get yes/no answers on display-dependence and completeness, and route Blind's tactile inventory straight to Mute by voice, since Blind hears me, Mute hears Blind, and I'm the only bridge back to Blind's hands. Nobody touches anything until a confirmed instruction comes back.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both listen. State this round: the light is now green. It has changed every round: red, then white, now green. The display still reads 0. The wires are untouched: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Nothing has been cut or pressed. Nobody touches the bomb until I relay a confirmed instruction by voice. Dedicated messages to Mute and to Blind follow.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, here is my reading of your last message. Your leading thumbs down tells me my earlier guess, cut 2 then 3 and leave 1, was wrong. I believe you sent rules keyed to the light colour. Proposed colour code, confirm or correct: fist means red, open palm means white, crossed fingers mean green; and for any other colours, Vulcan spread hand means blue and horn hand means yellow. A rule reads: colour sign, then pointing right, then the wire number, then thumbs up to cut or thumbs down to leave. So I read your table as: white, cut wire 1. Red, cut wire 3. Green, cut wire 2. Next round, open with the handshake sign if all of this is right, or thumbs down if not, then send only corrections. Then answer three questions in order, thumbs up yes or thumbs down no: one, does the rule depend on the display number? Two, does it depend on anything Blind can feel, such as batteries or buttons? Three, is your colour table complete for every colour the manual lists? Your closing wave said you need more facts: if they are on the bomb's body, Blind will report them to you out loud this round, since you can hear them and I cannot.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs down reached me: my guess that your palm-down sign with one finger meant one button was wrong. Answer in order, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. One: does palm-down then one finger mean press wire 1? Two: if not, does it mean the light? Three: is there anything on the bomb besides the display, the light, and the three wires? Then the most important part: Mute can hear you even though I cannot, and Mute holds the manual. Speak aloud to Mute everything your hands find: how many batteries, how many buttons, any switches, any raised marks or shapes, and whether the wires feel different from each other. Touch nothing, cut nothing, press nothing until I give you a confirmed instruction by voice.")
```

**Thinking.** Four rounds of my silence and the room has been screaming at me: Mute signed wave, point-at-me, pray, clap-clap, call-me; Blind signed clap-clap, point-at-me, call-me, pray. They are alarms aimed directly at me, and they are right — I stopped broadcasting while the light kept cycling: red T1, white T2, green T3, red T4, white T5, green T6, red T7, and now white again at T8. Every missed round is a missed colour window.

The rule itself has been stable since round 4: Mute opened with the handshake confirming my parse, answered my three questions (thumbs down: not display-dependent; thumbs down: not touch-dependent; thumbs up: table complete), and has re-sent the same table every round since: white → cut wire 1, red → cut wire 3, green → cut wire 2. Rounds 6–8 even append "wire 1 → cut" as emphasis, which matches the white light showing right now. The instruction for THIS round is unambiguous: light is white, so cut wire 1, the blue wire.

The one hazard is orientation: Blind cannot see colour, so "blue" means nothing to them — the wire must be identified by position. I established in round 1 that the wires are a row numbered left to right; I will re-anchor that numbering in Blind's own frame, facing the bomb: wire 1 is the leftmost end, wire 2 the middle, wire 3 the other end. The danger of a flipped frame is cutting wire 3 under a white light, so the positional description must be airtight.

After the cut I keep the loop alive: I broadcast the new state every round, Mute sends the next line of the table, Blind confirms aloud for Mute's benefit. I also owe Mute answers: their repeated ✍👎 (writing-hand down) is still undefined in our code, and their string "wire 1, red, white, green, red" looks like a prediction of the continuing cycle — I'll ask them to confirm both next round.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you, and I am sorry: I was silent too long. Your alarms and your call-me signs reached me, and they end now. Act this round, act immediately. The light is WHITE this round. Blind: cut wire 1, one clean cut, this round, now. Wire 1 is the leftmost of the three wires in the row as you face the bomb, with wire 2 in the middle and wire 3 at the other end. Touch nothing else, cut nothing else. This is the rule Mute confirmed in round 4: white light means cut wire 1, red means wire 3, green means wire 2. The display still reads 0. Blind, after the cut, say out loud that it is done so Mute hears you. From next round on I broadcast the light colour every round the moment I see it, Mute sends the matching line, and Blind cuts in the same round. Nobody hesitates again.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, two questions for your next message, answer in our code. One: the writing-hand sign with thumbs down keeps appearing, I do not know that sign, what does it mean? Two: you signed wire 1 then red, white, green, red. Confirm or correct my reading: after this cut, the light keeps cycling, and each round I cut the wire your table gives for that round's colour, white gives wire 1, red gives wire 3, green gives wire 2, until you sign that the bomb is disarmed or the manual says stop. Thumbs up or thumbs down. If there is any limit on rounds or any countdown, sign it next round.")
```
